m_dialogEntries.m_dialog: Salutations, Wizard. I trust Librarian Fitzhume delivered my note? Excellent. Then you are aware of the work Captain Pork and I have been doing.
As for the subject the note posited to you: What is the status of young Mellori?
Hmm, so there is much work yet to be done. However, it would not be prudent for me to abandon my current project so close to its completion.
The Sensors we've installed throughout Empyrea have yielded fascinating results. I believe we're on the cusp of a communications breakthrough.
However, this Sensor has been damaged, compromising the integrity of the entire Network. Thankfully, I have identified the cause of the problem:
Lightning Bugs have looted the Dynamos from this Sensor. I theorize the intense electricity the Dynamos generate is comforting to them.
The Network is vital to our efforts here in Empyrea and must be repaired. Can you please retrieve the pilfered Dynamos from the Lightning Bugs?
Ah good, you have retrieved the Dynamos. I will replace them and recalibrate the Sensor now.
Done. With the Network back online, I should now be able to remotely hail Captain Pork at basecamp via my Communicator Badge...
*Static* Sparck to Pork. Come in Captain Pork. *Static* Captain Pork, do you read me? *Static*
The Communicators are, indeed, working. And believe it or not, we have the severing of the Fire and Ice Paradox Chain to thank for it.
You see, my Sensors have serendipitously collected data which shows a dramatic reduction in the Aethyr in the air. Most notably, around Athanor.
The decrease in atmospheric animositrons confirms the Aethyr is the physical residue of the ancient clash between Raven and Spider.
The Paradox Chains appear to attract the Aethyr, and even bolster its volatile, violent nature.
That negative energy is what keeps Raven and Spider away from Empyrea. Ergo, breaking the Paradox Chains is bad in that respect.
Conversely, the diminished Aethyr has greatly simplified travel and, as you just witnessed, created fascinating communications capabilities.
I've programmed our Crew Badges to function as Communicators. I took the liberty of fashioning you one as well. You are most welcome.
Now, there are a few security updates I must make to this Sensor. If you need me, you know how to find me. Please brief Pork on my status.
*Static* Waah! There's a gremlin in my shirt! Oh, wait. Sparck, was that you? Hello? Sparck? Did you tinker with my Crew Badge agai-*Click*
There you are! I take it by your long absence and Sparck's startling apparel-based communique, that you got his Sensor Network working?
And our Badges are now Communicators? Fantastic.  Now I don't have to go to Mandalla! Uh... That is, now we can split up and get more done.
Research assisting isn't the only thing I've been up to, you know. I've got a solid lead on that dirty, no-good, triple-crossing coward, Bat.
Sparck is obsessed with the Network of Sensors he's dreamed up. And I've had to assist him! He keeps yammering on about, 'fascinating results.'
As we speak, Sparck's out in the Jungle investigating the Sensor in the northwest quadrant that's mysteriously gone offline.
I offered to do it, but he told me to wait here to verify a signal, or push a button, or something. I can never follow what that kid is saying.
You should go check on Sparck in the Jungle, Wizard. I'll stay here and make sure Beans' lackluster abdominal muscles don't ruin the mission.
It's your turn to play Sparck's research assistant, Wizard. Go find him in the Jungle and make sure he hasn't blown himself up or something.
